questions.question: Which of the following is a common adaptation that helps prey animals avoid being hunted by predators?
options: Having very large, sharp tearing teeth
Being active only at night (nocturnal)
Having extremely bright and easy-to-spot colors
Being unable to run or move quickly

questions.question: Which set of physical features is most commonly associated with predator adaptations?
options: Good camouflage and being entirely herbivorous
Dull senses, slow movement, and thick shells
Big teeth, excellent eyesight, and fast running speed
Large flat grinding teeth and underground nesting habits

questions.question: Why does the bioaccumulation of toxic substances pose the greatest danger to top predators in an ecosystem?
options: Top predators have weaker immune systems than producers.
Toxins build up in higher concentrations as they are passed up the food chain.
Toxins are only manufactured inside the bodies of top predators.
Top predators absorb toxins directly from the air much faster than other species.

questions.question: Which agricultural practice is a major contributor to the bioaccumulation of toxic chemicals in food chains?
options: Crop rotation with legumes
Using organic compost on soil
Hand-weeding crop fields
Applying synthetic pesticides to protect crops

questions.question: A habitat is best described as a place where plants and animals live, containing which two components?
options: Only living (biotic) organisms
Only non-living (abiotic) elements
Both living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) parts
Only plants and soil nutrients

questions.question: What is a likely consequence if the physical environment of a habitat undergoes a rapid, drastic change?
options: Organisms will immediately evolve new genes to thrive.
It may become much harder for resident organisms to survive there.
All species in the habitat will immediately become producers.
The habitat's biodiversity will automatically double to compensate.

questions.question: Why are humans and other animals classified as consumers in an ecosystem?
options: They cannot make their own food and must eat other organisms.
They produce their own food using sunlight through photosynthesis.
They only break down dead matter in the soil without eating.
They do not require any energy to survive and grow.

questions.question: In a food chain diagram, what do the pointing arrows directly represent?
options: The direction in which animals migrate during winter
The transfer of biomass from one organism to another
The physical movement of predators chasing prey
The release of oxygen into the atmosphere

questions.question: What does a food web diagram represent within an ecological community?
options: A single linear sequence of who eats whom
Several interconnected food chains showing complex feeding relationships
The physical nests made by spiders to trap flying insects
The total number of trees present in a single forest habitat

questions.question: Why are all consumers ultimately dependent on producers for survival?
options: Producers clean the water supply for the consumers to drink.
Producers make all the food that supports the rest of the food chain.
Producers hunt down predators to keep consumers safe.
Producers provide consumers with shelter from harsh weather.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of events leading to a plant producing edible seeds and fruits?
options: Photosynthesis occurs, then pollen is transferred from stigma to anthers.
Pollen is transferred from the anthers of flowers to the stigma.
Seeds are dispersed by birds before flowers are formed.
Roots absorb minerals, which instantly transform into ripe fruit.

questions.question: How do plants and animals show mutual dependence when it comes to reproduction and survival?
options: Plants hunt animals for nutrients, while animals use plants for camouflage.
Plants provide oxygen, while animals provide carbon dioxide only.
Plants rely on animals like insects for pollination and birds for seed dispersal.
Animals rely on plants to clean their fur, while plants rely on animals to dig soil.

questions.question: Why are pollinators critical for ensuring human food security?
options: They directly consume agricultural pests that destroy crops.
They fertilize the soil with essential mineral nutrients.
They ensure that enough crops are pollinated to produce food for the human population.
They increase the amount of rainfall in farming regions.

questions.question: What is the definition of biodiversity?
options: The total number of individual plants in a single square meter
The number of different species that live in a particular place
The rate at which energy is transferred up a food chain
The process of animals migrating to warmer climates

questions.question: Which of the following explains why maintaining biodiversity is important for humans?
options: It guarantees that the climate will never change.
It keeps habitats healthy and provides resources like food and medicines.
It reduces the number of predators in the wild.
It allows farmers to grow crops without using any water.

questions.question: How can humans conserve the genetic diversity of plants for the future?
options: By replacing all wild habitats with uniform crop fields
By storing seeds in seed banks and other gene banks
By cross-breeding only a single species of flower worldwide
By removing all insects from agricultural areas

questions.question: Some pesticides used by farmers are designed to kill weeds. How does this help crops grow?
options: It increases the amount of shade over the crops.
It removes competing plants so crops get more resources like light and water.
It directly injects mineral nutrients into the crop roots.
It attracts more insect pollinators to the crops.
